Use the embedding `ENNReal.ofNNReal : NNReal → ENNReal` and the characterization of nonnegative infinite sums as suprema of finite subsums.

First establish the common lemma
\[
\operatorname{Summable}(f)\iff \sum_b \operatorname{ofNNReal}(f b)\ne\infty.
\]
The forward direction follows by coercing the finite NNReal sum; conversely, a non-top ENNReal `tsum` bounds every finite subsum, and this finite bound yields convergence of the monotone net of NNReal partial sums.

Then prove domination: from `g b ≤ f b`, monotonicity of `ofNNReal` and of the ENNReal `tsum` gives
\[
\sum_b \operatorname{ofNNReal}(g b)
\le
\sum_b \operatorname{ofNNReal}(f b)<\infty.
\]
Apply the common lemma to conclude `Summable g`. The essential feature is nonnegativity, which makes finite partial sums monotone and turns summability into boundedness away from `∞`.
